steps.title: Insert the incident
steps.text: The new critical incident is stored with a generated id.

steps.title: Trigger picks a radius
steps.text: trg_notify_nearby_users_on_incident runs AFTER INSERT and calls trg_fn_broadcast_incident_alert. The CASE on severity returns 10000 m for critical.

steps.title: Find nearby users
steps.text: User 3 is the reporter and is excluded. User 1 is about 9.3 km away and inside the 10 km radius. User 2 is about 14 km away and outside it.

steps.title: Write the alert
steps.text: One incident_alert row is inserted for user 1 with the distance and a formatted message.

steps.title: Notify listeners
steps.text: Because at least one alert was created, pg_notify publishes the incident id, severity, radius and recipient count on the incident_alerts channel.

steps.title: Trigger picks a radius
steps.text: Low severity falls through to the ELSE branch of the CASE, so the radius is only 1000 m.

steps.title: No user is close enough
steps.text: User 2 is the reporter. Users 1 and 3 are tens of kilometers away, far outside 1 km.

steps.title: Nothing is written
steps.text: The INSERT ... SELECT matches zero rows, so incident_alert stays unchanged. matched_count is 0, so pg_notify is skipped too.

steps.title: Insert with severity NULL
steps.text: severity is nullable and has no default, so it is stored as NULL.

steps.title: NULL falls to ELSE
steps.text: CASE NEW.severity matches no WHEN branch for NULL, so the radius becomes 1000 m.

steps.title: Find nearby users
steps.text: User 1 is the reporter. User 3 is about 560 m away and inside the radius. User 2 is far away.

steps.title: Alert uses a default severity
steps.text: COALESCE replaces the NULL severity with low in the alert row and in the message text.
